primitives.name: Weak-to-strong scheduling paradox
primitives.verbatim_quote: The most peculiar phenomenon in present day football lies in the willingness and even eagerness of weak elevens to schedule their opening games against far stronger ones.
primitives.assumptions: Zero-sum competition, information asymmetry, risk-seeking behavior under uncertainty.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Catastrophic early losses depleting morale and resources, preventing meaningful development for later games.

layer2.mapping: Captures the concept of 'strategic vulnerability' in GSI's risk-adjusted odds models and GSE's opponent selection heuristics, where early exposure to strong opponents serves as a high-variance signal for system calibration.
layer2.telemetry: Observing win/loss patterns in early-season schedules relative to end-of-season performance rankings.
